body.x: BlueSignum (CEO Hailey Yoon) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.
BlueSignum was born from the vision of creating a service that can help people spend each day with a better state of mind, from as close as possible.

At the trade show, they showcased Lighthouse, which has completed beta testing and was just released. Lighthouse, an AI-based mental health management solution, can help lower company turnover rates and maximize satisfaction tailored self-care activities. Unlike services that connect people with consultants, Lighthouse uses technology to calculate more reasonable prices and goes beyond simple meditations, providing various content and a wide range of solutions.

It uses various types of data to analyze the user’s traits and situation and uses this analysis to provide personalized treatment content. The therapy content delivered in a chatbot format, can be adjusted and changed according to the responses of the user, and can make personalized daily quests and short activities accordingly. The ultra-personalized algorithm chooses the most appropriate content from over 500 usable contents.

To this end, it uses not only user input in a machine learning-based predictive and analytic model, but also uses other passive digital expression data to calculate the user’s symptoms and psychological resources. In addition, it uses time series analysis and deep learning models from the data accumulated on the app to improve the quality of its recommendations.

BlueSignum chose the ability to affordably give access to treatment 24 hours a day with just a mobile device to improve the safety and quality of life of the user as Lighthouse’s greatest function. Lighthouse’s content library includes around 10 categories of psychological treatment, and each content can be customized so that users can have an ultra-personalized user experience. Each content responds to user input and changes to fit the user’s preferences, allowing users to have a more personalized and effective experience.

The company explained Lighthouse can provide very accurate diagnoses and recommendations through data collected from user input and phenotypes. It has the characteristic of being able to accurately and comprehensively determine the user’s needs and preferences by creating a more complex recommendation algorithm using additional data accumulated through app use instead of solely relying on information from its own reports.

Sang Lee, the COO of BlueSignum, explained that, “Our company covers both B2B and B2C services. In addition to services provided to B2C clients, Lighthouse provides overall employee utilization and key content statistics to our business clients. We also separately provide management tools that can check such types of information, excluding personal information of course. Wherever team members may be, they can use ‘Lighthouse’ to conveniently receive activities that are appropriate for them.”

She went on to say, “Lighthouse aims to provide the most ultra-personalized psychological content. Using a chatbot format, you can easily gain psychological knowledge and receive activity solutions that suits you. Lighthouse will provide more advanced recommendations as more data builds up,” and shared future plans, saying, “Going through a beta launch at the end of 2022, Lighthouse seeks to be closer to consumers in 2023 and enter the SaaS-based B2B industry.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
